name: Periods/PMS
description: Cycle changes, period pain, heavy or irregular periods and PMS symptoms.
fact: For most adults a cycle of about 21 to 35 days is considered typical, but it can vary from person to person.

name: PCOS/PCOD
description: Living with polycystic ovary syndrome or disease: symptoms, tests, lifestyle and treatment experiences.
fact: PCOS is one of the most common hormonal conditions in women of reproductive age, and many people go undiagnosed for years.

name: Pregnancy
description: Questions and experiences from early pregnancy to delivery.
fact: Regular antenatal check-ups help doctors spot and manage problems early.

name: Postpartum
description: Recovery, feeding, sleep and emotional wellbeing after having a baby.
fact: Mood changes after birth are common, and support is available. You do not have to cope alone.

name: Fertility
description: Trying to conceive, fertility tests, treatments and the emotional side of the journey.
fact: Fertility depends on both partners, and many causes can be treated. A doctor can advise when to get tested.

name: Menopause
description: Perimenopause and menopause: hot flashes, sleep, mood and life after menopause.
fact: Menopause is confirmed after 12 months without a period, and symptoms can start years earlier during perimenopause.

name: Thyroid
description: Hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism, Hashimoto's and understanding thyroid reports.
fact: Thyroid conditions are more common in women, and a simple blood test such as TSH is how they are usually checked.

name: Endometriosis
description: Pain, diagnosis, treatment and day-to-day life with endometriosis.
fact: Endometriosis is often diagnosed late. A symptom diary can help your doctor understand what you are feeling.

name: Mental Wellbeing
description: Stress, anxiety, low mood and looking after your mind alongside your body.
fact: Hormonal changes across the cycle, pregnancy and menopause can affect mood. Talking to someone can help.

name: Breast Health
description: Breast changes, screening, check-ups and support during tests or treatment.
fact: Knowing how your breasts normally look and feel helps you notice changes to mention to your doctor.

name: UTI
description: Urinary tract infections: symptoms, prevention and recurring infections.
fact: UTIs are very common in women. Burning or frequent urination is worth getting tested early.

name: Anemia
description: Low hemoglobin or iron: tiredness, diet, tests and follow-up.
fact: Iron-deficiency anemia is common in women, especially with heavy periods. A blood test confirms it.
